sd_botany_bay_a_k_a_the_stadium.blurb: A steep limestone amphitheater in Spearfish Canyon, a few miles up-canyon from the town of Spearfish, with 19 sport routes and a short walk from the road. The crag splits into an upper tier of long overhanging lines and a lower tier of shorter pitches. The grades lean hard: roughly a dozen routes sit in the 5.12 to 5.13 range, three go into the 5.14s, and only a couple fall at 5.9 to 5.11. Facing south and sheltered, it bakes in summer sun but is at its best in the cold months, when the low sun warms the wall. Not a spot for beginners or for hot afternoons.

sd_court_house_wall_the.blurb: The Court House Wall is a high-quality sport wall within the Shadowlands, at the upper end of Spearfish Canyon, and holds some of the hardest lines in the canyon. All 19 routes are bolted, and the climbing is both powerful and technical. Nothing here is easy: the grades run from 5.11 into the 5.14s, with the bulk at 5.12 and a handful at 5.13. Shadowlands faces north to northwest and stays shaded until late in the day, so the wall makes a good summer choice and a cold one in other seasons. A short walk along the traverse trail, then a fork down the hill, brings you to the base.

_expect.name: Euphamiah Beresford Memorial Wall a.k.a. "The Butt Rocks Wall"

sd_euphamiah_beresford_memorial_wall_a_k.blurb: A sport wall on the Sunshine side of Spearfish Canyon, reached by a faint trail that leaves the main Sunshine parking area and climbs toward a small painted marker for the crag. Its 18 routes cover the middle of the grade range: a single 5.9, a few 5.10s, and most of the rest in the 5.11s with a handful of 5.12s, so it suits climbers moving up from moderates as well as those warming up for harder lines. The wall loses sun a bit earlier than neighboring Sunshine walls, which helps on warm days. Spring and fall are the comfortable seasons. Poison ivy can be a nuisance in high summer.

sd_middle_marker_area.blurb: Middle Marker is a large, intricate formation in the Needles near Mount Rushmore, visible from Highway 244 and reached by following the trail straight up a wide gully, with the smaller Inner Marker tucked behind it. Eighteen routes mix sport (11) and trad (7), so a rack and quickdraws both come in handy; a couple of lines are two pitches. Grades start at the easy end of 5.6 and run up through a few 5.11s, but the weight is at 5.9 and 5.10, which makes this a good fit for solid moderate climbers. Routes are spread around the formation from the north face to the south face.
